scenes.subtitle: Same webhook, two different pipelines
scenes.narration: Both versions of the review bot answer the same merge request events. This video shows where they differ, and why.

scenes.title: What both versions share
items: GitHub and GitLab support
The same webhook and credentials
The same security scanner
One summary comment per review
scenes.narration: Both versions support GitHub and GitLab. They share the webhook, the credentials, the security scanner, and they post a summary comment.

steps.narration: Every merge request event arrives at the same webhook, whichever version the repository uses.
The repository setting decides the path. Version one code never checks this setting at all.
Repositories set to version two never enter version one code. They take their own path, end to end.
Either way, the result lands as a comment on the merge request.

scenes.title: Context version one builds
items: Git diff and a knowledge graph
Jira ticket context
The previous review
A security scan
scenes.narration: Version one reads the diff, a knowledge graph of the code, the Jira ticket, and the previous review of the same merge request.

scenes.title: Context version two builds
scenes.narration: Version two builds its own context from the changed lines, the code that calls them, the files in risk order, and a security and dependency scan. It has no knowledge graph and no Jira.

scenes.title: How the score is set
items: Version one: out of ten, set by the model
Version two: out of one hundred, set by code
Version two: the model nudges it by two at most
Version two: counts come from database rows
scenes.narration: Version one asks the model for a score out of ten. Version two computes a score out of one hundred from the issues in the database, and the model can only nudge it by two points.

scenes.label: Files version two must inspect before submitting
scenes.narration: Version two refuses to submit until it has inspected at least eighty percent of the risk ranked files. Version one has no such gate.

scenes.title: Reliability
items: Version one: a Redis lock per merge request
Version two: one active job per merge request
Version two: resumes after a worker crash
Version two: tracks tokens and cost per run
scenes.narration: Version one uses a Redis lock. Version two keeps one active job per merge request in the database, resumes after a crash, and tracks tokens and cost for each run.

scenes.title: Features only one version has
scenes.narration: Only version one has the fix bot, which writes and pushes fixes. Only version two lets a person triage an issue, and it runs shadow comparisons.

scenes.title: Where things stand
items: Both pipelines are live today
Each repository is served by one of them
Shadow mode runs version two without posting
Version two is not a full replacement yet
scenes.narration: Both pipelines are live today. Each repository is served by one of them, and shadow mode lets version two run quietly beside version one before any switch.
